text.p: Italian debt markets ended higher after an active day in which the December Btp future on LIFFE surged to yet another record peak at 126.55.
Profit taking began to set in by the end of trade leaving the December future only 53 basis points up on the day at 126.18 and the July 2006 Btp 59 basis points higher at 107.69.
The spread of 10-year Btps over the benchmark 10-year Bund held at 191 basis points after closing in below 190 basis points earlier in the day.
The lira tripped to 1,012.00 per mark before recovering on the back of the dollar to 1,008.50 later.
"The market is betting on the 1997 budget being approved and on a general positive scenario," one trader said.
Dealers said however the market could pull back to 126.00 which was viewed as an opportunity to buy.
"The market is currently tied to the Bund market although its gaining more than the German market," another noted.

On the domestic front, the government intends to go it alone in pushing the 1997 budget bill through the lower house of parliament after the centre-right opposition rejected a move to resolve differences on the legislation.
